subtopic: Attention backward / Memory footprint and recomputation
learningObjective: Reason about the peak activation memory of standard attention backward and how FlashAttention-style recomputation changes it.
stem: Consider the backward pass of standard attention O = softmax(Q @ K^T / sqrt(d)) @ V for shapes Q, K, V ∈ [B, H, N, d]. Select all correct statements about activation memory and recomputation. (Choose all that apply.)
codeSnippet:
# Forward:
# S = Q @ K^T / sqrt(d)                # [B, H, N, N]
# P = softmax(S, dim=-1)               # [B, H, N, N]
# O = P @ V                             # [B, H, N, d]

# Backward (given dO):
# Need dQ, dK, dV. Naive requires materialized P (or S).

options.text: FlashAttention avoids storing P in HBM by re-tiling backward: it stores only per-row (m, l) statistics from forward (size O(B*H*N)) and recomputes P block-by-block from Q, K in backward, trading extra compute for a large HBM saving.

In FlashAttention backward, the extra recomputation makes total FLOPs strictly larger than the forward-only baseline; the wall-clock speedup comes entirely from reduced HBM traffic dominating the extra compute.

The naive backward stores the softmax output P (or S) of shape [B, H, N, N] from forward and re-uses it in backward; this dominates activation memory for long sequences (quadratic in N) and is the main reason non-flash attention runs out of memory at long context.

The backward gradient of softmax with respect to logits requires access to the full P matrix element-by-element; there is no way to avoid materializing P in HBM at some point in any correct algorithm.

explanation: A is correct: naive backward keeps the [B, H, N, N] attention matrix from forward for use in dS/dV, dS/dQ, dS/dK; this activation dominates memory and prevents long-context training. C is correct: FlashAttention's backward recomputes P block-by-block using the stored (m_i, l_i) row statistics plus Q, K — the [B, H, N, N] matrix is never HBM-resident. D is correct: the recomputation adds FLOPs compared to a forward-only kernel; the wall-clock win comes from HBM I/O reduction dominating. B is wrong: FlashAttention explicitly shows you can compute gradients block-by-block without materializing the full P.

optionExplanations.B: Correct: FA backward is a compute-for-I/O trade.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: standard attention backward memory footprint.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: block-wise recomputation avoids full P materialization.

assumptions: Discussion is training attention with standard cross-entropy loss upstream.
'Naive backward' means a straightforward autograd derivation without I/O-aware fusion.
nonImplications: Does not imply that all attention backward implementations recompute; some do checkpoint P.
Does not imply that recomputation is always the best trade; on short sequences, storing P may be preferable.

performanceClaim.scope: Attention backward activation memory and FlashAttention recomputation trade
